newsitem.title: USA: DuPont buys high-oil corn rights.
newsitem.headline: DuPont buys high-oil corn rights.

text.p: DuPont Co said it purchased all business and technology rights for high-oil cron from Pfister Hybrid Corn Co and Holden's Foundation Seeds Inc for undisclosed terms.

DuPont said it had the right to secure Holden's share of the high-oil corn technology should ownership of Holden's change. Monsanto Co announced plans in January to acquire Holden's. "Although Holden's ownership will change, we plan to continue our research collaboration with DuPont, as well as our commitment to supply our seed customers with high-oil corn products," said President Ron Holden.

Pointing out the nutritionally improved grains business is "embryonic," DuPont spokesman Dan Hammes said he doubted there would be any antitrust problems cooperating with a Monsanto unit as "there is no mature business out there" in the market.
Pfister President Jim Crowley said the company will continue to develop and market seed corn varieties under the Pfister brand.
"We view this as a means to expand the Optimum high-oil corn research program. This will enable Pfister to continu to supply...a continuing flow of improved high-oil products.

High-oil corn is the platform for DuPont'S Quality Grains business, the company pointed out, noting it had shared the rights with the two companies. DuPont's grains "business includes Optimum high-oil corn, the fastest-growing nutritionally improved grain product in the United States," the company said.

Noting about 80 percent of U.S. corn production is for animal feed, DuPont explained that high-oil corn "contians significantly mnore energym, protein and key amino acids than commodity corn, which benefits the livestock industry, and ultimately consumers, by improving production efficiency and reducing costs." ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710))
